text:
alex_m: Hey team, customer hitting repeated 413 on embeddings endpoint when they stream large batches. They split by documents but still fail after ~50MB. Error: HTTP 413 Payload Too Large.
priya_s: Ugh. Are they using chunked transfer or assembling on client then sending?
alex_m: They're using streaming/chunked upload (transfer-encoding: chunked) to avoid holding whole payload in memory. Code snippet they sent: ```
fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers: {'Authorization': 'Bearer ...'}, body: streamReadable })
```
jamal_r: Any proxy or gateway in front of Redwood? 413 could be nginx / gateway limit.
sara_ops: Customer on our hosted API in eu-west. No custom proxy on their side reported. Our edge LB has 64MB default body limit but we bump per-client on request if needed. We'll check logs.
eng_oncall_bot: [auto] Ingesting request ID 01A2B3C4 for 1940001122 - size=52428800 bytes - returned 413 by upstream (nginx)
alex_m: They said the failure is intermittent: succeeds for smaller batches, fails for larger ones even split across chunks.
priya_s: Could be how chunk boundaries form - if client sends huge single chunk header lines or a very long chunk extension? But unlikely. Ask for raw curl repro.
jamal_r: Also check embedding dimension mismatch errors — sometimes client retries with different model or dims cause odd 413s if request format changes. Any dim mismatch logged?
alex_m: No dim mismatch yet in our logs. Only 413 and a few 502s when retries happened.
sara_ops: From logs: upstream nginx hit client_max_body_size for some connections. We have a per-route config but it didn't apply due to ALB re-route to static route. Will patch config but need interim workaround.
priya_s: Interim actions: 1) Recommend chunk size <= 8MB per chunk. 2) Use line-delimited JSON streaming (ndjson) with smaller documents per chunk. 3) Add retry/backoff on 413 with chunk-size reduction.
alex_m: Customer asked for precise repro steps we can run. I have their Node stream code. I'll try a curl streaming repro.
jamal_r: Example curl streaming pattern: ```
# stream file in 4MB chunks
python -c "import sys;import time;f=open('big.ndjson','rb');
import sys
while True:
 chunk=f.read(4*1024*1024)
 if not chunk: break
 print(chunk.decode('utf-8',errors='ignore'))
 time.sleep(0.1)" | curl -v -H 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d @-```
priya_s: Also add a header X-Request-Id for tracing.
sara_ops: Patch deployed to edge to honor per-route client_max_body_size — should reduce 413s. Deployed in 5m.
eng_oncall_bot: [auto] Patch rollout started to eu-west route.
alex_m: Sent repro curl to customer. They ran it and still saw occasional 413s but much less.
priya_s: If they still see occasional 413s, suggest: 1) enable content-length fallback instead of chunked when client can buffer, 2) or implement a simple multipart upload pattern: split payload into N smaller requests and server-side assemble embedding batches.
jamal_r: For multipart approach, we have a /v1/embeddings/append endpoint variant internally used by some customers — not public. Suggest use client-side batching: call embeddings in parallel with batch_size ~ 256 items (or ~2-4MB payload each) and then concatenate vectors client-side.
alex_m: Customer concerned about throughput impact. Any perf numbers?
priya_s: On our infra, smaller concurrent batches (256) with concurrency 8 gives near-linear throughput and avoids single huge payloads hitting LB size limits. Quantize for memory: 1M tokens => many small requests better than single giant one.
sara_ops: Follow-up: we added monitoring for chunked uploads and will alert if edge returns >1% 413s per minute.
support_bot: Case #CS-3582 escalated to Eng; assigned to jamal_r.
jamal_r: I'll look into making a public guidance doc: 'Streaming large embedding uploads - recommended patterns' with examples (curl, node, python) and recommended chunk sizes / retry logic.
alex_m: Great. For now I'll advise customer to: reduce chunk size to <=8MB, add X-Request-Id, implement retry on 413 with exponential backoff and halve chunk size on retry, or switch to small parallel batch uploads.
priya_s: Also ask them to log Content-Length vs Transfer-Encoding and paste any raw request headers if it fails again.
alex_m: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
eng_oncall_bot: [auto] Thread 1940001122 closed by eng_oncall after patch verification.
